1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ because God wanted it, and Sosthenes our brother.

To the church of God at Corinth. To those who are sanctified (made holy) in Christ Jesus, called to be saints (holy people). And to all in every place who call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both their Lord and ours:
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.
I always thank my God for you, because of the grace of God that is given to you by Jesus Christ.
In everything you are made rich by Christ, in all your speaking and in all your knowledge.
The testimony (witness) of Christ was confirmed (proven true) in you.
So you are not lacking in any gift, as you wait for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Christ will also confirm (make strong) you to the end. Then you will be blameless (without blame) in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful. God called you into the fellowship (sharing) of His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

Now I beg you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: all of you speak the same thing. Let there be no divisions among you. Be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
My brothers and sisters, people from the house of Chloe told me about you. They told me there are contentions (fighting) among you.
This is what I mean. One of you says: I follow Paul. Another says: I follow Apollos. Another says: I follow Peter. Another says: I follow Christ.
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified (put to death on a cross) for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
So that no one can say that I baptized in my own name.
I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Besides them, I do not know if I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel (good news). I do not preach with wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ will not lose its power.
For the preaching of the cross is foolishness to those who perish. But to us who are saved, it is the power of God.
For the Scripture says: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. I will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent (clever).
Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe (teacher of the law)? Where is the debater of this world? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?
In the wisdom of God, the world did not know God by its own wisdom. So it pleased God to save those who believe, by the foolishness of preaching.
The Jews ask for a sign, and the Greeks look for wisdom.
But we preach Christ crucified (put to death on a cross). To the Jews this is a stumbling block. To the Greeks it is foolishness.
But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than people, and the weakness of God is stronger than people.
Look at your calling, brothers and sisters. Not many of you were wise by human standards. Not many were mighty. Not many were noble.
But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound (shame) the wise. God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound (shame) the mighty.
God has chosen the base (lowly) things of the world, and the things that are despised (looked down on). God has even chosen things that are nothing, to bring to nothing the things that are.
God did this so that no one should glory (brag) in His presence.
Because of God you are in Christ Jesus. God has made Christ to be our wisdom, righteousness (being right with God), sanctification (being made holy), and redemption (being bought back and set free).
So, as the Scripture says: Whoever glories (brags), let them glory (brag) in the Lord.

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: And I, brothers and sisters, when I came to you, did not come with excellency (fancy) of speech or of wisdom. I came telling you the testimony (witness) of God.
For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified (put to death on a cross).
I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
My speech and my preaching were not with enticing (persuasive) words of man's wisdom. They were in demonstration (proof) of the Spirit and of power.
This was so that your faith would not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
Yet we speak wisdom among those who are perfect (fully grown). But it is not the wisdom of this world, or of the princes (rulers) of this world, who come to nothing.
We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery (secret), the hidden wisdom. God ordained (planned) it before the world began, for our glory.
None of the princes (rulers) of this world knew this wisdom. If they had known it, they would not have crucified (put to death on a cross) the Lord of glory.
But as the Scripture says: Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered into the heart of man, the things God has prepared for those who love Him.
But God has revealed (shown) these things to us by His Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.
What man knows the things of a man, except the spirit of man that is in him? In the same way, no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God. This is so that we can know the things God has freely given to us.
We also speak these things, not in the words that man's wisdom teaches, but in the words the Holy Spirit teaches. We compare spiritual things with spiritual things.

But the natural man (a person without God's Spirit) does not receive the things of the Spirit of God. These things are foolishness to the natural man. The natural man cannot know them, because they are spiritually discerned (understood only through the Spirit).
But the one who is spiritual judges all things. Yet no one judges the spiritual person.
For who has known the mind of the Lord, so that he can instruct (teach) the Lord? But we have the mind of Christ.

verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I could not speak to you as to spiritual people. I spoke to you as to carnal (ruled by the sinful self) people, as to babies in Christ.
I fed you with milk, not with meat (solid food). Before, you were not able to take it. And even now you are still not able.

For you are still carnal (ruled by the sinful self). There is envying (jealousy), strife (fighting), and divisions among you. Are you not carnal (ruled by the sinful self), and living like ordinary men?
For one of you says: I follow Paul. Another says: I follow Apollos. Are you not carnal (ruled by the sinful self)?
Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos? Paul and Apollos are only ministers (servants) through whom you believed, as the Lord gave to each one.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase (made it grow).
So the one who plants is not anything, and the one who waters is not anything. God is the One who gives the increase (makes it grow).
The one who plants and the one who waters are one. Each one will receive their own reward, according to their own labor (work).
For we are laborers (workers) together with God. You are God's husbandry (farm field). You are God's building.
By the grace of God given to me, I have laid the foundation, like a wise master builder. Another person builds on it. But let each one be careful how they build on it.
For no one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Someone may build on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or stubble (dry stalks of grain).

Each person's work will be made manifest (shown clearly). The day will declare (show) it, because it will be revealed (shown) by fire. The fire will try (test) each person's work, to see what kind it is.
If anyone's work that they built on the foundation abides (lasts), they will receive a reward.
If anyone's work is burned, they will suffer loss. But they themselves will be saved, yet as through fire.
Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells (lives) in you?
If anyone defiles (ruins) the temple of God, God will destroy the person who defiles it. For the temple of God is holy, and you are that temple.
Let no one deceive (fool) themselves. If anyone among you seems to be wise in this world, let them become a fool, so that they may be wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For the Scripture says: He takes the wise in their own craftiness (tricks).
And again: The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain (empty).
So let no one glory (brag) in men. For all things are yours,
Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Peter, or the world, or life, or death, or things now, or things to come. All are yours.
And you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.
Let people think of us as ministers (servants) of Christ, and stewards (managers) of the mysteries (secrets) of God.
Also, it is required in stewards (managers) that they be found faithful.
But to me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man's judgment. Yes, I do not even judge myself.
For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified (shown to be right) by this. The One who judges me is the Lord.

So judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes. The Lord will bring to light the hidden things of darkness. The Lord will make manifest (show clearly) the counsels (plans) of the hearts. Then each person will have praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I have used myself and Apollos as an example, for your sakes. I did this so you can learn from us not to think of men above what is written. Then none of you will be puffed up (proud) for one person against another.
For who makes you different from another? What do you have that you did not receive? If you did receive it, why do you glory (brag), as if you had not received it?
Now you are full. Now you are rich. You have reigned as kings without us. I truly wish you did reign, so that we also could reign with you.
For I think God has set us apostles last, like men appointed (sentenced) to death. For we are made a spectacle (show) to the world, to angels, and to men.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are despised (looked down on).
Even to this very hour we are hungry and thirsty. We are naked (without enough clothes), and we are buffeted (beaten). We have no settled home.
We labor (work hard), working with our own hands. When we are reviled (insulted), we bless. When we are persecuted (attacked for faith), we suffer it (put up with it).
When we are defamed (lied about), we intreat (answer kindly). We are made like the filth (dirt) of the world. We are the offscouring (garbage) of all things to this day.
I do not write these things to shame you. I warn you as my beloved (dear) sons.
For though you have ten thousand instructors (teachers) in Christ, you do not have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus I have begotten you (become your father) through the gospel (good news).
So I beg you, be followers of me.
For this reason I have sent Timothy to you. Timothy is my beloved (dear) son, and faithful in the Lord. Timothy will bring to your memory my ways in Christ, as I teach everywhere in every church.
Now some of you are puffed up (proud), as though I would not come to you.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills. Then I will know, not the speech of those who are puffed up (proud), but their power.
For the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod (a stick for punishment), or in love and in the spirit of meekness (gentleness)?

verses.text: It is commonly reported that there is fornication (sexual sin) among you. It is such fornication (sexual sin) as is not even named among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). One of you has his father's wife.
And you are puffed up (proud). You have not mourned instead, so that the man who has done this deed would be taken away from among you.
For I truly, as absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged the man who has done this deed, as though I were present.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together, and my spirit is with you, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Deliver (hand over) such a man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh (sinful self). Then the man's spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your glorying (bragging) is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven (yeast) spreads through the whole lump of dough?
So purge out (clean out) the old leaven (yeast), so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened (without yeast). For even Christ our passover (Passover lamb) is sacrificed for us.

So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven (yeast), or with the leaven (yeast) of malice (hate) and wickedness. Let us keep it with the unleavened bread (bread without yeast) of sincerity (with an honest heart) and truth.
I wrote to you in a letter not to keep company with fornicators (people who do sexual sin).

Yet I did not mean that you must stay away altogether from the fornicators (people who do sexual sin) of this world, or the covetous (people who want what belongs to others), or extortioners (cheaters), or idolaters (people who worship idols). For then you would need to go out of the world.

But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone called a brother who is a fornicator (person who does sexual sin), or covetous (wanting what belongs to others), or an idolater (person who worships idols), or a railer (person who insults others), or a drunkard, or an extortioner (cheater). Do not even eat with such a person.
For what do I have to do with judging those who are outside the church? Do you not judge those who are inside the church?
But God judges those who are outside the church. So put away from among yourselves that wicked person.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Does any of you dare, when you have a matter against another believer, to go to court before the unjust, and not before the saints (holy people)?
Do you not know that the saints (holy people) will judge the world? If the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life?
So if you have cases about the things of this life, set those who are least esteemed (thought of) in the church to judge them.
I say this to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you? Is there not one who will be able to judge between his brothers?
But brother goes to court against brother, and that before the unbelievers.
Now there is utterly (completely) a fault among you, because you go to court against one another. Why do you not rather take the wrong? Why do you not rather allow yourselves to be cheated?
No, you do wrong, and you cheat, and you do it to your own brothers.

Do you not know that the unrighteous (people who are not right with God) will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived (fooled). Fornicators (people who do sexual sin), idolaters (people who worship idols), adulterers (people who have sex with someone else's husband or wife), the effeminate (men who give themselves to other men for sex), abusers of themselves with mankind (men who have sex with men),
Thieves, the covetous (people who want what belongs to others), drunkards, revilers (people who insult others), and extortioners (cheaters) will not inherit the kingdom of God.
And some of you were like this. But you are washed. You are sanctified (made holy). You are justified (made right with God) in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.
All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but all things are not expedient (helpful). All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

Meats (foods) are for the belly, and the belly is for meats (foods). But God will destroy both the belly and the meats (foods). Now the body is not for fornication (sexual sin), but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
And God has both raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by His own power.

Do you not know that your bodies are the members (parts) of Christ? Should I then take the members (parts) of Christ, and make them the members (parts) of a harlot (prostitute)? God forbid (no, never).
What? Do you not know that whoever is joined to a harlot (prostitute) is one body with her? For He says: The two will be one flesh (body).
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit with the Lord.
Flee (run away from) fornication (sexual sin). Every sin that a person does is outside the body. But whoever commits fornication (sexual sin) sins against their own body.
What? Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own.
For you are bought with a price. So glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V36-38 follow the KJV's 'giveth her in marriage' (a father and his unmarried daughter), not the modern text's 'marries'.

verses.text: Now about the things you wrote to me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.
But to avoid fornication (sexual sin), let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give to the wife the kindness that is due to her. And in the same way let the wife give it to the husband.
The wife does not have power over her own body, but the husband does. And in the same way the husband does not have power over his own body, but the wife does.

Do not defraud (hold back from) one another, except with consent (agreement) for a time, so that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan does not tempt you because of your incontinency (lack of self-control).
But I say this by permission, and not as a commandment.
For I wish that all men were even as I myself am. But every man has his own gift from God, one in this way, and another in that way.
So I say to the unmarried and to widows: It is good for them if they stay even as I am.
But if they cannot contain (control) themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn (with desire).
And to the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord: Let not the wife depart from her husband.
But if she does depart, let her stay unmarried, or be reconciled (made peace) with her husband. And let not the husband put away (divorce) his wife.
But to the rest I speak, not the Lord: If any brother has a wife who does not believe, and she is pleased to live with him, let him not put her away (divorce her).
And the woman who has a husband who does not believe, if he is pleased to live with her, let her not leave him.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified (made holy) by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified (made holy) by the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean. But now they are holy.
But if the unbeliever departs, let the unbeliever depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage (slavery) in such cases. But God has called us to peace.
For how do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O man, whether you will save your wife?
But as God has given to every person, as the Lord has called every one, so let each one walk (live). And this is what I ordain (order) in all churches.
Was any man called when he was already circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Was any man called while uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing. What matters is the keeping of the commandments of God.
Let every person stay in the same calling in which they were called.
Were you called while you were a servant (slave)? Do not let it worry you. But if you can be made free, use it rather.
For whoever is called in the Lord while a servant (slave) is the Lord's freeman. In the same way, whoever is called while free is Christ's servant.
You are bought with a price. Do not be the servants (slaves) of men.
Brothers and sisters, let every person stay with God in the place where they were called.
Now about virgins (people who have never married): I have no commandment from the Lord. Yet I give my judgment, as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.
So I think this is good because of the present trouble. I say it is good for a person to stay as they are.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be loosed (set free). Are you loosed (free) from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But such people will have trouble in the flesh (in this life). But I want to spare you.
But this I say, brothers and sisters: the time is short. From now on, let those who have wives be as though they had none.
Let those who weep be as though they did not weep. Let those who rejoice be as though they did not rejoice. Let those who buy be as though they did not own anything.
And let those who use this world be as not abusing (misusing) it. For the fashion (way) of this world is passing away.
But I want you to be without carefulness (worry). The unmarried man cares for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord.
But the married man cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

There is a difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But the married woman cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
I say this for your own profit (good). It is not to put a snare (trap) on you. It is for what is comely (fitting), so that you may serve the Lord without distraction.

But if any man thinks he is acting uncomely (not rightly) toward his virgin (his unmarried daughter), if she is past the flower of her age (the best age to marry), and need requires it, let him do what he wants. He does not sin. Let them marry.

But the father who stands stedfast (firm) in his heart, having no necessity (need), and has power over his own will, and has decided in his heart that he will keep his virgin (his unmarried daughter), does well.
So then the father who gives her in marriage does well. But the father who does not give her in marriage does better.
The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives. But if her husband is dead, she is at liberty (free) to be married to whom she wants, only in the Lord.
But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment. And I think also that I have the Spirit of God.

Now I will write about meat that is sacrificed to idols. It is certainly true that we all have knowledge. But this knowledge only fills people with pride. It is love that helps the church grow stronger.
Those who think they know something do not yet know anything as they should.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
Now I want to talk about meat that has been sacrificed to idols. We all know that no idol in the world is alive. We know that there is only one true living God.
Many people say there are gods in heaven or on earth. We know that people worship many gods and say they are lords.

For us there is only one God, and He is our Father. All things came from the Father, and we live for Him. And there is only one Lord, Jesus Christ. All things were made through Him, and we also have life through Him.

But not all the believers understand that there is only one God. They served these idols for many years before they became believers. They think that when they eat meat that was sacrificed to idols, they serve those idols. And because these believers feel guilty very easily, they think that they have sinned.
But food will not bring us closer to God. Refusing to eat does not make us less pleasing to God, and eating does not make us closer to Him.
Some of you think it is not wrong to eat meat that was sacrificed to idols. Be careful. Other believers may sin when they see what you eat.

Suppose you believe it is not wrong to eat meat sacrificed to idols. Now suppose someone with weak faith sees you eating in an idol's temple. That person may think they too can eat there. They may even start serving those idols.
Their faith is not strong, and because you think it is not wrong to eat meat that was sacrificed to idols, they may be lost. But they are a believer, and Christ died for them.
When you do something that would make other believers feel guilty, then you sin against Christ.
That is why I make this choice. Suppose food makes a fellow believer sin. Then I will never eat meat again. I will never make other believers sin.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. No errors found.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Am I not completely free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord with my own eyes? Are you believers not the result of my hard work for the Lord?
Even if others do not accept me as an apostle, surely you do, for you yourselves are the proof that I am an apostle in the Lord.
This is my answer to those who question me.
Do we not have the right to food and drink?
Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as the other apostles do, and the Lord's brothers, and Peter?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who must work to support ourselves?
Who serves as a soldier and pays their own way? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its grapes? Who takes care of a flock and does not drink its milk?
Am I only saying this from a human point of view? Does the law not say the same thing?
The Law of Moses says: Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes grain. Was God thinking only about farm oxen? No, He was definitely speaking about us!
The worker who plows the field expects to eat from the harvest. The worker who threshes the grain expects a share of the crop.
If we have planted spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to receive some material help from you?
If others have this right to be supported by you, do we not have it even more? But we have not used this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than get in the way of the good news of Christ.
Do you not know that those who work in the temple get their food from the temple? Those who serve at the altar share in what is offered there.
In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the good news should make their living from it.
But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this so that something will be done for me. I would rather die than let anyone take away this thing I am proud of.
For when I preach the good news, I cannot brag, because I am required to do it. How terrible it would be for me if I did not preach the good news!
If I preach because I choose to, I have a reward. But even if I do not choose it, I have still been trusted with this job.
So what is my reward? Just this: when I preach the good news, I can offer it free of charge. So I do not make full use of my rights as a preacher.
Though I am free and belong to no one, I have made myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

When I was with Jewish people, I lived like a Jew. I did this to lead Jewish people to Christ. When I was with people under the Law, I followed their customs. I am not trapped under that Law myself. I only did it to bring those people to Christ!
When I was with Gentiles who do not have the Law, I lived like them. This does not mean I ignore God's commands. I follow the Law of Christ!
To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all possible means I might save some.
I do all this for the sake of the good news, so that I may share in its blessings.
Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? So run in such a way as to win the prize.
Everyone who competes in the games trains hard in everything. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
So I do not run like someone with no finish line. I do not box like a fighter just punching the air!
I discipline my body strictly, like a dedicated athlete. I make my body obey me! I do this so that after preaching to others, I will not fail the test.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I do not want you to forget that all our ancestors were under the cloud, and all of them passed through the sea.
They were all united under Moses as their leader. The protecting cloud covered them, and they walked through the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and they all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual Rock that went with them, and that Rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, and their bodies were scattered over the desert.
These things happened as examples for us, to keep us from setting our hearts on evil things as they did.
Do not worship idols, as some of them did. The Scripture says: The people sat down to feast and drink. Then they got up to dance in wild, sinful worship!
We should not commit sexual sin, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
These things happened to them as examples, and they were written down as warnings for us, on whom the end of the ages has come.
So if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you do not fall.

Every temptation you face is common to all human beings. And God is completely faithful to you! He will not let you be tempted beyond your strength. When temptation comes, He will provide a clear way out. Then you will have the strength to stand strong!
So, my dear friends, run away from the worship of idols.
I am speaking to you as sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.
When we drink from the blessed cup, we thank God. Do we not share together in the blood of Christ? When we break the bread, do we not share together in His body?
There is one single loaf of bread. Though we are many people, we form one united body!
Think about the people of Israel: those who eat the sacrifices share in the altar, do they not?
So what am I saying? That an idol is anything, or that food offered to an idol is anything?
No, but the sacrifices of those who do not know God are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to share with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too. You cannot share in the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than He is?
Some people say: I am allowed to do anything. But not everything is good. Some people say: I am allowed to do anything. But not everything builds people up.
No one should look out only for their own good, but also for the good of others.
Eat anything that is sold in the meat market, without asking questions for the sake of your conscience,
for: The earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.
Suppose someone who does not believe invites you to a meal, and you want to go. Eat whatever is put before you. Do not ask questions for the sake of conscience.
Suppose someone at dinner warns you: This meat was offered to an idol. Then do not eat that meat!
Do this for the sake of the person who told you. Do it to protect that person's sensitive conscience. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I eat with thankfulness, why am I blamed for something I thank God for?
So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God.
Do not cause anyone to stumble: not the Jews, not the other nations, and not the church of God.
This is what I do: I try to please everyone in every way. I am not looking out for my own good, but for the good of many, so that they may be saved.

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
I praise you for remembering me in everything and for holding on to the teachings, just as I passed them on to you.
I want you to understand God's order of authority. Christ is the head of every man. The husband is the head of the wife. And God the Father is the head of Christ!
A man dishonors Christ when he prays with his head covered.
A woman dishonors her husband when she prays with no veil. That is just as shameful as shaving off all her hair!
If a woman refuses a veil, she might as well shave her head. Since a shaved head brings shame, she should wear a head covering.
A man should not cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man.
For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.
And man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
For this reason, and because of the angels, a woman should have a sign of authority on her head.
But in the Lord, woman is not separate from man, and man is not separate from woman.
For just as woman came from man, so man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it right for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that it is a shame for a man to have long hair,
but that long hair is a woman's glory? For her hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no such practice, and neither do the churches of God.
Now in giving these instructions I cannot praise you, because your meetings do more harm than good.
First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
No doubt there have to be differences among you, to show which of you have God's approval.
When you gather, you do not really eat the Lord's Supper.
Each rich person rushes ahead and eats their own private meal. Poor people go hungry while others get completely drunk!
Do you not have your own homes for eating and drinking? You are humiliating the poor and insulting God's church! Should I praise you for this? I definitely will not!
I passed on to you what the Lord Jesus gave me. On the night someone betrayed Him, the Lord Jesus took bread.
He thanked God and broke the bread into pieces. He said: This is my body, broken for you. Eat this bread to remember me.
After supper, He took the cup in the same way. He said: This cup is the new agreement in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me!
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you are showing the Lord's death until He comes.
Do not treat the Lord's bread and cup with disrespect. Anyone who does that sins against the Lord's body and blood!
Every person must examine their own heart before eating.
Respect the body of the Lord when you eat. Disrespecting it brings God's judgment upon yourself.
That is why many among you are weak, sick, and dying.
But if we judged ourselves truly, we would not be judged.
When the Lord judges us, He is correcting us, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home, so that when you meet together it will not bring judgment. And when I come, I will give further directions.
Now, brothers and sisters, I want you to understand about spiritual gifts.
Remember the lives you lived before you were believers. You let yourselves be influenced and led away to worship idols, things that have no life.

That is why I tell you: If the Spirit of God is in someone's heart, that person cannot curse Jesus. And when someone believes that Jesus is the Lord, they can say that only because the Holy Spirit is in their heart.
There are different gifts, but it is the same Spirit who gives them.
And there are different ways to serve the Lord, but we serve the same Lord.
And there are different kinds of ways that God works in the congregation, but it is the same God who helps people do all these things.
The Spirit shows everyone what they must do, because the Spirit knows what is best for the congregation.
The Spirit gives one person the ability to speak with wisdom. And the same Spirit gives another person the ability to speak with knowledge.
The same Spirit gives faith to one person, and to another He gives gifts of healing.

To another person, the Spirit gives the power to do miracles. To another, He gives the ability to prophesy God's message. To another, He gives the power to tell true spirits from fake spirits. To another, He gives the ability to speak in unknown languages. And to another person, He gives the ability to interpret those languages.
One Spirit, the same Spirit, does all these things. The Spirit decides what to give each one.
Every person has a body, but that body has many parts. Yes, there are many parts, but the many parts are one body. It is the same with the body of Christ. It has many parts.
When we were baptized, the Holy Spirit made us all part of one body. We are Jews, Greeks, slaves and free people but the same Spirit is in all of us.
Our bodies do not have only one part. They have many parts.
Suppose the foot says: I am not a hand, so I do not belong to the body! That does not stop the foot from being part of the body.
Suppose the ear says: I am not an eye, so I do not belong to the body! That does not stop the ear from being part of the body either.
If the whole body were an eye, then the body would not have been able to hear. And if the whole body were an ear, then the body would not have been able to smell.
But now God has given different parts to the body. He gave every part as He wanted.
If the whole body were just one part, then it would not have been a body.
But now there are many parts, and there is only one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand: I do not need you. The head cannot say to the feet: I do not need you.
We think there are parts of the body that are weaker than other parts, but the body needs them.
And the parts that we think are not worth very much are the parts we give the most care to. And we give special care to the parts of the body that we do not want to show.
The more beautiful parts do not need this special care. But God put the body together and gave more honor to the parts that need it.
That is why the body does not fight against itself, because the different parts of the body care for each other.
When one part of the body suffers, then all the other parts also suffer. And when the people praise one part of the body, then all the other parts are also happy.
All of you together are the body of Christ. You all are a part of this body.

God placed different people in the church for special work. First, He appointed apostles. Second, He appointed prophets. Third, He appointed teachers. Next come those who perform miracles and those who heal the sick. Then come those who help others, those who lead, and those with different tongues.
Is everyone an apostle? No! Is everyone a prophet? No! Is everyone a teacher? No!
Can everyone perform miracles or heal the sick? No! Does everyone speak in unknown tongues or interpret them? Of course not!
Continue to give your attention to the spiritual gifts you consider to be the greatest. But now I want to point out a way of life that is even greater.

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. No errors found.

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: If I speak in the languages of people and even of angels, but do not have love, I am only a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
I may have the gift of prophecy. I may understand all secrets and all knowledge. I may have faith strong enough to move mountains. But if I do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own, and even give my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. Love is not jealous. It does not brag, and it is not proud.
It is not rude. It does not look out only for itself. It does not get angry easily, and it keeps no record of wrongs.
Love is not glad about evil, but is glad about the truth.
Love always protects, always trusts, always hopes, and always keeps going.
Love never ends. But prophecies will stop, other languages will cease, and knowledge will pass away.
For we know only a part, and we prophesy only a part.
But when what is perfect comes, what is only a part will pass away.
When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I grew up, I put childish ways behind me.
For now we see only a dim picture, as in a poor mirror. But then we will see face to face. Now I know only a part; then I will know fully, just as I am fully known.
So these three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Run after love, and also long for the gifts of the Spirit, especially the gift of prophecy.
For anyone who speaks in another language is not speaking to people but to God. No one understands them; they are speaking secrets by the Spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people to build them up, encourage them, and comfort them.
The one who speaks in another language builds up themselves, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.

I want all of you to speak in unknown languages. Even more, I want you to prophesy God's truth! A person who prophesies helps the church more than someone speaking in tongues. Tongues help only when someone interprets the words to build up the church.
Now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in other languages, how does that help you? It helps only if I bring you some message, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching.
Think about lifeless musical instruments like a flute or a harp. If the notes are not clear, no one recognizes the tune!
If the bugle does not blow a distinct call, who will prepare for war?
It is the same with you. Unless you speak words that are easy to understand, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
There are surely many different languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
But if I do not understand the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and that person will be a foreigner to me.
It is the same with you. Since you are eager for the gifts of the Spirit, try to do well at building up the church.
So anyone who speaks in another language should pray that they can explain what they say.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind does not understand.
So what should I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
Suppose you praise God only in an unknown spiritual language. How can an ordinary visitor say Amen to your prayer? They have no idea what you are saying!
You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in other languages more than all of you.
But in the church I would rather speak five words that people understand, to teach others, than ten thousand words in another language.
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking. Be like babies when it comes to evil, but be grown-ups in your thinking.
In the law it is written: With other languages and other lips I will speak to this people. But even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.
So other languages are a sign, not for believers but for those who do not believe. But prophecy is for believers, not for those who do not believe.
Suppose the whole church meets and everyone speaks in unknown tongues. If unbelievers or visitors walk in, they will call you crazy!
But suppose everyone is prophesying God's clear truth. When an unbeliever enters, the words will convict their heart!
God will expose the secret thoughts inside them. They will fall face down, worship God, and say: God is truly here!

So what should you do, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each of you has a song, a teaching, another language, a message from God, or an explanation. Everything must be done to build up the church.
If anyone speaks in another language, two, or at most three, should speak, one at a time, and someone should explain.
If there is no one to explain, the speaker should keep quiet in the church and speak only to themselves and to God.
Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
And if a message comes to someone sitting nearby, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all prophesy, one at a time, so that everyone can learn and be encouraged.
Prophets must control their own spiritual speech.
God does not author wild confusion; He brings peaceful order!
The women should keep quiet in the churches. They are not allowed to speak, but should be submissive, as the law also says.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home, because it is a shame for a woman to speak in the church.
Did the word of God begin with you? Or are you the only people it has reached?
If anyone thinks they are a prophet or a spiritual person, they should recognize that what I am writing to you is the Lord's command.
But if anyone ignores this, they will be ignored.
So, my brothers and sisters, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in other languages.
Everything done in your meetings must be orderly and respectful.
Now, brothers and sisters, I want you to remember the gospel I told you. You received that Good News, and you continue to base your life on it.
That Good News, the message you heard from me and believed, is God's way to save you. Do not change the word which I preached to you, unless you believed in vain (without complete commitment).
I, Paul, gave you the message that I received. I told you the most important truths: that Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures say.
Jesus was buried and Jesus was raised to life on the third day, as the Scriptures say;
Jesus appeared to Peter, then to all twelve apostles.
Later Jesus appeared to more than 500 of His followers at once, most of whom are still alive, although some have died.
Then Jesus appeared to James and later to all the apostles.
Last of all, Christ appeared to me, Paul! I was like a baby born at the wrong time.
I am the least important of all the apostles. I do not even deserve the name apostle! Why? Because I violently attacked God's church.

Because of God's grace, I am an apostle now. God's grace that He gave me was not wasted. I worked harder than all the other apostles. (But I was not really the one working. It was God's grace that was with me.)
It is not important who preaches to you, I or the other apostles. What is important is that we all preach the same message and that you believe it.
We tell everyone that Christ was raised from death. So why do some of you say that people will not be raised from death?
If no one will ever be raised from death, then Christ has never been raised.
And if Christ has never been raised, then the message we tell is worth nothing. And your faith is worth nothing.

If the dead never rise, we lied about God! We officially testified that God raised Christ from the dead. But God did not raise Christ if dead people never wake up! And if the dead do not rise, then Christ stayed dead, too!
If those who have died are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if God did not make Christ live again, then your faith is worth nothing, and you are still guilty of your sins.
Then everyone who belonged to Christ and has died is lost.
If we hope that Christ saves us only for this life on earth, then everyone must feel very sorry for us.
But our message is true: God has raised Christ from death to live again, this is sure. Christ is the first One who died and was raised to live again.
Death came into the world through one human man, Adam. In the same way, the resurrection comes through one Man, Christ!
Everyone dies because we are connected to Adam. In Christ, all believers will be brought back to life!
But everyone will be raised to life in the right order. Christ was first to be raised. Then, when Christ comes again, those who belong to Him will be raised to life.
Then the end will come. Christ will destroy all rulers, authorities, and powers. Then He will give the kingdom to God the Father.
Christ will rule until God has defeated all enemies of Christ and put them under His feet.
The last enemy that Christ will defeat is death.

It is written in the Old Testament: God put everything under Christ's control. When God says that everything is put under Christ, it is clear that this does not include God Himself. God is the One putting everything under Christ's control.

God will place everything under the rule of Christ. Then Christ the Son will place Himself under God the Father. God is the One who gave Christ total authority. In the end, God will rule over everything and everyone!
If no one will ever be raised from death, then what will the people do who are baptized for those who have died? If the dead are never raised, then why are people baptized for them?
And what about us? Why do we put ourselves in danger every hour if the dead will not live again?
I swear, dear brothers and sisters, by the pride I have in you through Christ Jesus our Lord: I face death daily.
In Ephesus I fought wild animals. If I did that only for human reasons, then I have gained nothing. If we are not raised from death, then let us eat and drink, because tomorrow we die.
Do not let people deceive you. Bad friends will ruin good habits.
Come back to your right way of thinking and stop sinning. Some of you do not know God. I say this to shame you.
Some people ask: What will it be like when the dead people live again? What will their bodies look like?
Why do they ask these foolish questions? When you plant something, it must die in the ground before it can live and grow.
And when you plant something, what you plant does not have the same body that it will have later. What you plant is only a seed, maybe wheat or something else.
But God gives it the body that He has planned for it, and He gives each kind of seed its own body.
All things made of flesh are not the same: People have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds have another, and fish have yet another kind.
Also there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the beauty of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the beauty of the earthly bodies is another.
The sun has one kind of beauty, the moon has another kind, and the stars have another. And each star is different in its beauty.
It will be the same when those who have died are raised to life. The body that is buried in the grave will ruin and decay, but it will be raised to a life that cannot be destroyed.
When the body is buried it is without honor. But when it is raised, it will be great and glorious. When the body is buried, it is weak. But when it is raised, it will be full of power.
The body that is buried is a physical body. When it is raised, it will be a spiritual body. There is a physical body, and there is also a spiritual body.
In the Old Testament it is written: The first man, Adam, became a living person. The last Adam, Christ, became a life-giving spirit who restores the dead to life.
Remember, the spiritual body did not come first. The human body was first and after that, the spiritual body came.
God made the first man from the dust of the earth. But the second Man is the Lord from heaven.

People who belong to this world are like the first man. They are like the man who came from the earth. But people who belong to heaven are like the Man who came from heaven. Christ is the One who came from heaven.
Now we all are like the man of dust, but the time will come when we will be like the Man from heaven.
I tell you this, brothers and sisters: Our bodies of flesh and blood cannot have a part in God's kingdom. Something that will ruin cannot have a part in something that never ruins.
Listen, I will tell you a wonderful secret! Not all of us will die. Instead, God will instantly transform all of us!
It will happen in one second, faster than an eye blink. The final trumpet will blast loud and clear! The dead believers will wake up with bodies that never rot. And God will change all of us forever!
Because this body that we have now can become dust, God will give us a body that cannot become dust. This body that we have now can die, but God will give us a body that will never die.
God will give us a body that cannot die or become dust. Then the words in the Old Testament will come true. It is written: God has defeated death.
Death, where is your victory? Where is your power to hurt?
The power and sting of death come from sin, and the power of sin comes from the law.
But we thank God who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand strong. Do not let anything change you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord. You know that your work in the Lord is never wasted.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Two merged-verse numbering bugs (12/13, 15/16) have been split apart, and several typos/garbled sentences fixed (v2, v30, v44, v48).

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Now about the collection for God's people: do what I told the churches in Galatia to do.
On Sunday, the first day of the week, put aside some money. Save according to how much money you made that week. Do this so you will not rush to collect money when I arrive.
When I arrive, I will give letters of introduction to the people you approve, and send them to take your gift to Jerusalem.
And if it seems best for me to go too, they will go with me.
I will come to you after I go through Macedonia, for I am going to pass through there.
Maybe I will stay with you for a while, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
I do not want to see you only in passing. I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord allows.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
A wide door of great opportunity has opened for my work here! At the same time, many enemies actively oppose me.
When Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to fear while he is with you, because he is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So no one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he can come back to me. I am expecting him, along with the other brothers.
Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the others. But he did not want to go now; he will go when he has the chance.
Stay alert and watchful! Stand firm in your faith! Be courageous and bold! Be strong in the Lord!
And do every single thing with love.
You know the family of Stephanas. They were the very first believers in the region of Achaia. They dedicated their lives to serving God's people.
Follow the godly leadership of people like them. Respect everyone who works hard alongside them!
I was glad when Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus arrived, because they have made up for your absence.
They have refreshed my spirit, and yours too. So show your appreciation to people like them.
The churches in Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the church that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone does not truly love the Lord, God's curse is on them. Our Lord, come quickly!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
